# Psalm 49 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

## 49:1 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** For-the-choirmaster. Of-the-sons of-Korah. A-psalm.
- **LOGOS:** For the choirmaster. A psalm of the Sons of Korah.
- **PNEUMA:** For the music director. A psalm of the descendants of Korah.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 49:4 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** My-mouth speaks wisdom, and-the-meditation of-my-heart [is] understanding.
- **LOGOS:** My mouth shall speak wisdom; the meditation of my heart shall be understanding.
- **PNEUMA:** For my words are wise, and my thoughts are filled with insight.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 49:5 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** I-incline my-ear to-a-proverb; I-open with-the-lyre my-riddle.
- **LOGOS:** I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will solve my riddle to the music of the lyre.
- **PNEUMA:** I listen carefully to many proverbs and solve riddles with inspiration from a harp.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 49:7 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Those-trusting in-their-wealth and-in-the-abundance of-their-riches they-boast —
- **LOGOS:** those who trust in their wealth and boast of the abundance of their riches?
- **PNEUMA:** They trust in their wealth and boast of great riches.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

- **EMET:** But-man in-honor does-not endure; he-is-like the-beasts [that] perish.
- **LOGOS:** Man in his pomp will not remain; he is like the beasts that perish.
- **PNEUMA:** but their honors will not last. They will die, just like animals.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 49:17 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Do-not fear when-a-man grows-rich, when-the-glory of-his-house increases;
- **LOGOS:** Be not afraid when a man becomes rich, when the glory of his house increases.
- **PNEUMA:** So don't be dismayed when the wicked grow rich and their homes become ever more splendid.
